translations.answer: Suggest that each component use its own `CallbackQueue` so that `AsyncSpinner` handles the component's ROS API on a non-realtime thread; real-time and non-realtime threads should use `realtime_tools::RealtimeBuffer` for safe data exchange. Clarify two boundaries: changes to the environment should not trigger system calls on the real-time thread, and non-realtime threads should not lock shared resources required by the real-time thread.
translations.applicability: Applicable to ROS 1 ros_control callback/control cycle isolation; specific non-locking structures must be verified per version.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: Construct the hardware interface and ControllerManager in the RTT `configureHook()`, and execute `read → update → write` in the `updateHook()`.
translations.details.attempts.1: Establish an independent `CallbackQueue` for each component, spun by a non-realtime thread, and use `RealtimeBuffer` for data exchange.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Clearly mark the thread for each of `configure`, `read`, `update`, `write`, and `callback`, and verify that shared data is passed through real-time safe exchange structures.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Delegate cycle scheduling to real-time executors like RTT/HAL, and isolate ROS API callbacks on non-realtime threads.
translations.details.environments.0: ROS 1 ros_control; PREEMPT_RT/Xenomai discussion; Orocos RTT example; threads from 2013–2018.
translations.details.limits.0: The example is from an old ROS 1/RTT; `ros::Time::now()` has an old real-time safety issue in the same repository, so it cannot directly use the time source.
translations.details.limits.1: No unified WCET, jitter, or kernel comparison is available.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The thread participants publish the minimum `rtt_ros_control_example`; another user explicitly states these discussions helped develop `hal_ros_control`.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How to run the ros_control read-update-write cycle with an external real-time scheduler?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How to handle ROS callbacks and runtime parameters without blocking the real-time cycle?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Real-time WBC must pass parameters through boundary checks and atomic/reliable real-time safe exchange; non-realtime callbacks should not hold regular mutexes required by real-time threads.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Non-realtime callbacks and real-time cycle share a regular mutex, or real-time thread triggers setting changes and system calls, leading to priority inversion and unpredictable delays.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Mixing ROS callbacks, services, and control cycles in a single execution model leaves unresolved scheduling priority, mutexes, and system call boundary issues.
translations.source.title: Separate ros_control Realtime Cycle from ROS Callbacks and Services
translations.title: How to safely integrate ROS callbacks, services, and runtime settings with ros_control's real-time cycle without causing priority inversion?
